thread:
Emma (ML): Quick heads-up — rolled r3b-large-v2 ptq-int8 snapshot to shadowbench this morning. NDCG@10 is down ~3.2% vs fp16 baseline but MRR@10 is slightly up (+1.1%). Need triage, pinging the usual suspects.
Anya: @Emma (ML) can you paste the eval command and which holdout you used? :mag:
Emma (ML): sure — running with prod_holdout_v2, batch 64, seed 42. eval snippet:
```
./eval_rerank.py --model r3b-large-v2-int8 --holdout=prod_holdout_v2 \
  --batch 64 --seed 42 --cache-prefix-match
# summary (fp16 -> int8)
NDCG@10: 0.841 -> 0.814 (-3.2%)
MRR@10: 0.642 -> 0.649 (+1.1%)
n_queries: 120000
```
Emma (ML): No config changes on the harness other than loading int8 weights via ptq pipeline.
Mario: first-pass thought — is candidate ordering identical? small reorderings can blow NDCG but bump MRR if top-1 gets slightly better. Any de-dup or snippet changes upstream?
Ryan (Infra): were runtime flags identical? batching, kvpack, and autoreduce can change the kv cache timing. We should ensure eval runtime mirrors prod serving.
Emma (ML): offline harness uses stable ordering from search export. Prod candidates sometimes go through snippet-prune which can remove top candidates. But we used the same candidate dump; still worth checking.
ci-bot: CI: shadowbench job #592 completed with metrics artifact at s3://redwood-shared/shadowbench/592/metrics.json :white_check_mark:
Anya: plan: 1) slice by query length (short/medium/long), 2) disable kvpack and prefix cache in the runtime, 3) run with deterministic tie-break seed and compare ranklists. Any objections?
Emma (ML): sounds good. I ran a quick slice locally — weirdly the NDCG drop is concentrated on short queries (<20 tokens). quick output:
```
short (<20): NDCG@10 fp16 0.780 -> int8 0.720 (-7.7%)
medium (20-100): 0.845 -> 0.823 (-2.6%)
long (>100): 0.860 -> 0.849 (-1.2%)
```
Mario: that points at tokenization/priming differences or prompt truncation edgecase. Int8 execution shouldn't change tokenization but if we changed the tokenizer binary/version or switched to a slightly different BPE vocab that's likely. Also check normalization (html strip, whitespace).
Anya: could also be quantization-induced score compression that affects short queries where scores are tightly clustered. If int8 compresses scores, topk margin changes more for short queries. Can we dump raw logits for a few failing queries and compare distribution?
Ryan (Infra): I can spawn a parity run on a dedicated node with identical flags to prod (batching, kvpack on/off) and upload artifacts. ETA ~45m.
Emma (ML): Mario — can you diff tokenizer versions between baseline and the int8 build? Also run a small seed-limited eval (n=1000) that logs candidate order + tokens.
Mario: on it. I saw a packaging change in the int8 build that bumped tokenizers from 0.12.1 -> 0.12.3. I'll diff vocab checksums and run token dumps.
Anya: I'll run the ablations (kvpack off, prefix cache off, deterministic tie-break) and a logits-dump for 200 short queries. Will post a gist of rank diffs.
Emma (ML): awesome — let's regroup in 2 hours. If anyone finds a concrete repro (single query where ranks flip), paste the full candidate list + tokens. Action items: Anya=ablation+logits, Mario=tokenizer/vocab diff+seeded eval, Ryan=runtime parity run. I'll shepherd the notebook for quick triage. :eyes:
Ryan (Infra): noted, creating parity job now. Will post job link when ready.
ci-bot: CI: artifact upload complete for job #593 -> s3://redwood-shared/shadowbench/593/ (metrics + traces) :arrow_up_small:
Emma (ML): thanks all — if this ends up being quant-induced score compression we should consider a tiny calibration layer or bias-correction for short queries before rolling to dedicated/diff.
Anya: noted. If we confirm compression, I'll try a per-query-length rescale as a quick patch.
Mario: token diffs done — vocab checksum mismatch on the int8 packaging. uploading token dumps now.
Emma (ML): great, will start inspecting diffs. Reconvene 2h.
